full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J.-This Rule is directed as to show because why G.R. Case No. 143 of 1973 pending in the court of the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Brahamanbaria, should not be quashed. Facts giving rise to the proceedings are as follows:- 

 4. We are satisfied that the evidence does not disclosed that the leaves are smuggled goods. On the other hand there is evidence to show that Kumbhi leaves in. question were the produce of the garden of Mr. M.R. Bhuiya and the said gentleman had the necessary permit for dispatching them by railway wagon vide annexure 'C' and before that there was a survey report on 2-4-73 by the Divisional Authorised Officer. In this view of the matter it cannot be said that these Kumbhi leaves were smuggled and therefore our opinion is that no offence was committed by the accused petitioners. In this view of the matter interfere race at the initial stage of the proceeding is called for. In the case of Abdul Kader Vs. State, reported in 28 DLR 38, the appellate Division of the Supreme Court considered of certain categories for quashing and have expressed the opinion that if the facts do not constitute the offence as alleged then there is no question of appreciation of the evidence and therefore it would be legitimate for the High Court to hold that it would be ma infest unjust to allow process of the criminal court to be issued against the accused persons. Our attention has been drew to the case of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab reported in A.I.R. 1960 (SC) 866. It is to be noted that Indian Supreme Court had also made 3 categories and as to the category No. 2 Indian Supreme Court also has expressed the opinion that where the allegation in the First Information Report even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute He offence alleged, then no question of appreciating the evidence arise d and the High Court will be justified In quashing the proceeding, Fortified d with these two decisions and one of which is binding upon us we arc of the opinion that proceedings in S.G.R. Case No. 143/73 will be an abuse of the process of the Court and therefore should be quashed.
